notes_list.title: UV–Visible Spectroscopy — Chromophores and Conjugation
notes_list.basic_overview: UV–Visible spectroscopy measures electronic transitions; conjugated systems often show absorption at longer wavelength as conjugation increases.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Important transitions include π→π* and n→π*. Bathochromic shifts move λmax to longer wavelength; hyperchromic effects increase intensity.
notes_list.examples: Ethene absorbs at shorter wavelength than extended conjugated dienes; aromatic/conjugated chromophores show characteristic bands.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Solvent polarity can shift n→π* and π→π* bands differently; concentration is handled through Beer–Lambert law in the linear range.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Identify chromophore → determine possible electronic transition → compare conjugation/substitution → predict λmax and intensity changes.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: A = εbc. Deviations can arise from concentration, chemical equilibria, stray light and instrumental limitations.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not infer exact structure from λmax alone; UV gives limited but useful conjugation information.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
